changelog: Insert a single narrow, binding rule after C8 to keep a finite verb/auxiliary with its immediately following core complement (1–4 tokens). This directly addresses the primary finding that verb–complement splits produce orphaned arguments and entailment/confusion.

Insert one narrow binding after C8 to keep numerals/quantifiers attached to their immediately following unit/measurement (within four tokens); addresses the primary finding that splitting numeral+unit produces incoherent or contradicted short pieces.

Insert a single fallback ordering after C8 that, as a last resort, prefers punctuation/clause-boundary cuts over cuts that separate a finite verb/auxiliary from its immediately following core complement, and prefers those over cuts that split a numeral/quantifier from its immediately following unit/measurement — to protect verb–complement integrity (primary finding) while preserving the short-bin benefit of punctuation.

Insert a single fallback ordering after C8 that, as a last resort, prefers cuts that keep numeral/quantifier+unit together first, then keeps finite verb/auxiliary adjacent to its immediately following core complement, and only then prefers punctuation/clause boundaries — to protect numeral–unit integrity (primary finding) while retaining punctuation as a tiebreak.

Delete C5 — remove the temporal/subordinator protection because it largely duplicates scope/attachment protections already expressed (C3, C4, C8), has no measured gain, and pruning a redundant v0 principle should reduce rule competition and attention dilution.

Insert one narrow, binding principle after C8 to keep a finite verb/auxiliary adjacent to its immediately following core complement (within four tokens). This reproduces the measured target choices that keep verb+complement together and prevents orphaned arguments and entailment/confusion.

Insert one induced ordering after C8: prefer a cut immediately before a finite verb/auxiliary over a cut that falls between that verb and its immediately following core complement (direct object, essential prepositional object, or clausal complement) when that complement begins within the next 1–4 tokens — this reproduces the measured target choices without banning cuts and addresses the primary finding about verb–complement splits.
